# Metabolomics {#sec-metabolomics}

::: {.callout-note}
## What you should know before reading this chapter

This chapter assumes you are comfortable with the following.

- Basic mass spectrometry instrumentation and terminology, as covered in @sec-introduction.
- Chromatographic separation by LC and GC, at a conceptual level.
- Reading a chromatogram and a mass spectrum.

If any of these are unfamiliar, start with the linked material before continuing.

<!-- TODO: add links to external resources for each prerequisite. -->

The chapter is written for readers coming from either a wetlab or a computational background.
Sections that assume substantial knowledge of one or the other are marked at the top.
:::

<!--
Say what metabolomics is, how it differs from proteomics in scale and in the identification problem, and why the small-molecule case is harder to annotate.
Then explain how the subsections below fit together as a pipeline.
-->

This part covers the path from a raw acquisition to a reported, annotated metabolite table.

- @sec-feature-detection covers how a raw signal becomes a feature table.
- @sec-annotation covers how chemical identity is assigned to a feature, and with what confidence.
- @sec-databases-standards covers where the reference data lives and how results should be reported.

Stable isotope labeling and flux analysis build directly on this material and are treated separately in [Stable isotope labeling and flux analysis](../stable-isotope-labeling/index.qmd).
